payload.scope: A binaural spatialization cue representing the inter-ear time delay used to encode sound direction in computational audio processing.

definition.body: Interaural-time-difference is a computational parameter used in binaural audio rendering that encodes the time delay between sound arrival at two ears, computed from a virtual source position relative to a head model. payload.scope: A computational audio enhancement method that applies psychoacoustic masking thresholds across time-frequency bins to suppress noise and artifacts.

definition.body: Time-frequency-masking is a signal processing method that suppresses spectral components in a time-frequency representation based on psychoacoustic masking thresholds, computed from the spectral envelope and frequency selectivity of human hearing. definition.body: Cepstral-deresolution is a signal processing method that recovers high-resolution spectral detail suppressed by envelope-extraction or smoothing procedures, by inverting or compensating for quefrency-domain filtering. The procedure: (1) obtain the smoothed or envelope cepstrum c_env[q] via low-pass liftering; (2) obtain the full cepstrum c_full[q] of the original signal; (3) compute the residual: c_res[q] = c_full[q] - c_env[q], isolating fine spectral detail; (4) optionally enhance the residual via thresholding or normalization. The result is a detail component that, when added back to the envelope, reconstructs the full spectrum. Used in speech enhancement, source separation, and spectral recovery. Parameters: the lifter order (quefrency cutoff), the residual computation method, and the enhancement strategy. Persistence: implemented in speech processing research code and audio restoration toolkits. e.g.: the cepstral residual computed in the HTS-SPICE speech enhancement system for noise robustness; the quefrency-domain dereverberation using cepstral resolution in the ITU-T G.729 Annex Q standard; the cepstral detail component extracted in the NIST speaker recognition evaluation for fine speaker characterization [formal: resolucio cepstralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.scope: People made cepstral-rate to measure how quickly cepstral coefficients change between consecutive frames of an audio signal, capturing temporal dynamics of spectral change.

definition.body: Cepstral-rate measures how quickly cepstral coefficients change between consecutive frames of an audio signal, capturing the temporal dynamics of spectral change. The procedure: (1) compute cepstral coefficients c[n] for consecutive frames n and n+1; (2) compute the first difference delta[n] = c[n+1] - c[n]; (3) compute the L2 norm of delta[n] as the cepstral-rate, optionally weighted by quefrency-dependent factors to emphasize perceptually relevant coefficients. Parameters: (1) the input signal frames, (2) the number of cepstral coefficients M, (3) the frame shift in samples, (4) optional quefrency weighting. Parameters: (1) the input audio frames, (2) the number of cepstral coefficients M, (3) the silence threshold value, (4) the frame shift in samples. Persistence: used in speech recognition for VAD and silence trimming in Kaldi front-ends; in speaker diarization for silence segmentation in NIST evaluations; in audio processing for activity detection in HTK-based pipelines. e.g.: the cepstral-based VAD in Kaldi for automatic speech transcription silence trimming; the cepstral energy threshold in HTK for speaker diarization activity detection; the cepstral silence detection in Praat for automated speech annotation [formal: detectio silentii cepstralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

definition.body: Cepstral-drift measures systematic shifts in cepstral coefficient statistics over time, capturing gradual changes in acoustic environment, channel characteristics, or speaker state. The procedure: (1) compute cepstral coefficients for consecutive frames or windows; (2) track the mean and variance of each coefficient index over a sliding window; (3) compute the drift as the temporal derivative of the coefficient means, or the Mahalanobis distance between current and reference coefficient distributions. Parameters: (1) the cepstral coefficient sequence, (2) the reference statistics for drift comparison, (3) the window size for tracking, (4) the drift threshold for alerting. Persistence: used in speech recognition for adaptive cepstral normalization in Kaldi online processing; in speaker recognition for session variability compensation in NIST evaluations; in audio surveillance for acoustic environment change detection in HTK-based pipelines. e.g.: the cepstral drift adaptation in Kaldi for online speaker adaptation in streaming ASR; the cepstral distribution shift detection in HTK for session variability normalization; the cepstral drift metric in Praat for monitoring recording environment changes [formal: devium cepstrale | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]
